would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The result report's "To operate" prescribes bumping the LIVE `omegahive` run's generation as the way to verify registration, which is the one action the order bolds as never to be done and substitutes a mutating check for the read-only query evidence the order requires.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: Operator step 2 tells the operator to run `bump-generation --run-id omegahive` outside any restore, and shows the success output `generation bumped for 'omegahive': 1 -> 2` as the confirmation to look for. Following it forces every live coordinator, worker and notifier to take GENERATION_MISMATCH, drop its cursor and re-snapshot — exactly the harm the stop-line names ("a live bump forces every client to re-snapshot, and nothing in this order needs it"). It hits the live deployment's clients at the moment the operator follows the post-merge checklist, and it displaces the read-only `runs` query the order's DoD specifies for this very evidence ("query evidence in the report — read-only"). The scratch-run bump evidence the order does allow is already present in tests, so the live bump buys nothing.
